title: Input contracts
acceptance: Validate versioned synthetic payment, label and experiment schemas before work; reject unexpected fields and malformed timestamps.

title: Identity and scope
acceptance: Use organization plus synthetic identifier as every entity key; reject cross-organization scoring context.

title: Money
acceptance: Store nonnegative integer minor units and currency; compare amounts within one currency, never implicit currency conversion.

title: Time availability
acceptance: Features use only records available at scoring time and occurrences before the current event; equal-time cohorts cannot see each other.

title: Duplicate semantics
acceptance: Same payment ID and identical payload is one event; same ID with a different payload is a contract error.

title: Delayed labels
acceptance: Every supervised stage receives only resolved labels available by its own knowledge cutoff; training, selection, calibration and policy artifacts freeze before first final-test score.

title: Unknown outcomes
acceptance: Unresolved and censored outcomes remain unknown; metrics disclose denominators and maturity coverage.

title: Synthetic generator
acceptance: Generate legitimate and risky behavior from different probabilistic mechanisms with overlapping feature distributions, explicit seeds and original data.

title: Legitimate controls
acceptance: Include payroll, high-value purchases, new customers, shared payees and travel-like behavior as legitimate hard negatives.

title: Temporal split
acceptance: Freeze nonoverlapping chronological observation windows, maturity intervals, per-stage knowledge cutoffs, label coverage gates and all decision artifacts before final-test scoring.

title: Entity holdout
acceptance: Report a separate cold-entity/component test with disjoint synthetic actor components and no train-test graph edges.

title: Preprocessing
acceptance: Fit imputers, encoders, scalers, resampling and feature selection on eligible training only.

title: Behavior features
acceptance: Compute rolling counts and amounts, payee novelty and changes relative to permitted prior history with cold-start indicators.

title: Graph features
acceptance: Compute bounded local graph features from eligible historical edges; no future centrality or label-based graph contamination.

title: Baselines
acceptance: Run prevalence/random ordering, declared rules, regularized logistic regression and a tabular tree baseline on identical rows.

title: Candidate ablation
acceptance: Compare tabular features against behavioral and graph additions under equal tuning budgets.

title: Calibration
acceptance: Fit calibration on exclusive chronological rows and labels available by its own cutoff; calibration artifact freezes before policy and final-test scoring.

title: Review capacity
acceptance: Enforce a declared queue capacity and deterministic ties; operational top-K batch results are not called real-time blocking results.

title: Evidence output
acceptance: Return model version, score type, timestamps, reason features, uncertainty and counterevidence with no allegation.

title: Metric completeness
acceptance: Report precisely named resolved-subset metrics and population bounds, selected/unselected unknown counts, amount weighting and a paired component bootstrap that recomputes daily K and queues.

title: Cost model
acceptance: Report a known-outcome cost subtotal plus lower/upper full-population bounds covering both selected and unselected unknown payments; distinguish modeled from realized savings.

title: Subgroup assessment
acceptance: Report predeclared behavior and customer-age slices plus sample counts; suppress unsupported small-sample claims.

title: Drift
acceptance: Evaluate covariate and typology shifts plus delayed-feedback windows without automatic retraining on test labels.

title: Reproducibility
acceptance: Record code/data/split/feature/model hashes, environment, seeds, freeze cutoffs, configuration and failures.

title: Reviewer workflow
acceptance: Present a ranked offline queue and traceable evidence; record review outcome independently from model score.

title: Secure boundaries
acceptance: No network calls or live actions in R1; escape report content; deny untrusted executable model formats.

title: Performance measurements
acceptance: Measure end-to-end latency, memory and throughput on disclosed hardware; optimization cannot silently change feature semantics.

title: Research claims
acceptance: Record null results and limitations; no funding, novelty, award, certification or production-readiness claim without evidence.

title: Independent reproduction
acceptance: Reproduce deterministic fixtures and aggregate experiment results in a second clean environment with documented tolerance.

title: Public release control
acceptance: Publish only reviewed public artifacts and authorized sources; full sensitive methods, private data and operational thresholds stay outside a public export.
